title: S&P Global Investment Manager Index (Dec 2026) — the control month: same rule, CPI five days earlier, no collision
source: EST: DERIVED BY THE SAME RULE — the Tuesday eight days after the month's first Monday — which the never-assessed initial research of sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-11-10 took to 9 FOR 9 across 34 months (Dec 2023 through Sep 2026) on eight primary mastheads plus one calendar listing, six of those mastheads fetched direct on 2026-09-09, two of them (2023-12-12 `bef94184f0af457cb9ade4a6f00f7189` and 2026-03-10 `66f4aa2f5c60454eb5b2366efa1f4a39`) never read by any prior lane. December 2026's first Monday is 2026-12-07, giving 2026-12-15 (a Tuesday; all 72 rule outputs over 2021-2026 are Tuesdays, checked mechanically). TIME: 15:00 UTC = 10:00 EST, quoted rather than inferred — both EST-month mastheads in the read set state '1000 EST (1500 UTC)' verbatim (2023-12-12, 2026-01-13). S&P Global's PMI calendar (pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes) is a rolling [today+2, today+28] window running 'September 11' to 'October 07' today, so December cannot be read from it and will not be readable until roughly 2026-11-17. Proposed by the never-assessed initial research of sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-11-10, 2026-09-09. Estimate for the same single honest reason as its three siblings: no publisher statement of this date exists.
notes: PROPOSED AS THE CONTROL MONTH, AND AS THE LAST EDITION THIS LANE PROPOSES. The November lane's leg 3 found that the CPI collision on 2026-11-10 is STRUCTURAL rather than accidental: the rule can only ever output the 9th through the 15th of the month, near-uniformly (11/10/10/10/10/11/10 over 72 months), which is exactly the band BLS occupies — all four CPI dates this calendar tracks (2026-09-11, 10-14, 11-10, 12-10) fall inside the same seven-day window. December 2026 is the control that makes that claim testable rather than merely stated: same rule, same band, CPI on 12-10, and NO collision, because the weekday geometry pushes the IMI five sessions later. It is also the second EST-month edition in the calendar and therefore the second test of the fall-back time claim the November lane registered as FT-sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-11-10-2. NOT PROPOSED FOR THE TAPE, AND THE TAPE QUESTION IS CLOSED. The November lane doubled the sibling study to 68 rule-derived release days across 2021-2026 (SPY p=0.43, QQQ 0.80, TLT 0.56, `^TNX` 0.96) and scored the October lane's own kill switch — 'the 32-day null reverses on a longer daily sample' — which did not fire. Do not spend a session re-deriving it. NOT A TRADE: symbols is empty, no macro-keyed house playbook, no published consensus for a sentiment survey, status is estimate. THIS IS DELIBERATELY THE END OF THE CHAIN: the ladder's questions are complete at four editions (September clean / October sized-confound / November collision + election panel / December control), and an edition proposing its own successor every month would be a process defect rather than research. If the November listing appears on any date other than 2026-11-10, or at any time other than 15:00 UTC, this proposal is derived from a broken rule and should be corrected by whoever finds it.
